Game log, most recent first: 5, 9, 4, 2, 4, 1, 3, 7. Weighted average 4.7; went higher than 5.5 in 2 of 8 games (24% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 6.0 vs 3.4 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±2.5, so the line is 0.3 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Market: ESPN Bet make this side 56% once their cut is removed; Hard Rock's price needs 61%. Hard Rock charges more than the market for this side.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +2% on his average.
PFF: BAL plays man on 29% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 22%); he gains 2.63 yds/route vs man and 3.12 vs zone → -1% from scheme.
PFF: BAL allows 1.70 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.59) → +9% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 34% of his routes from the slot (2.54 yds/route there, 3.09 outside); BAL allows 1.54 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.74 outside (league 1.46 / 1.67, opponent-adjusted) → +6% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 4.7 catches on average; in a typical game 4.1 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 1.4 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 26% and the matchup 24%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 50%, matchup 54%.
Bottom line: we give it 54% to win and it needs 61%. The edge is the difference: -6.9 points; that works out to about -11¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
